answer: No. While the story contains a surprising turn—Ruth realizing she was given the wrong baby and choosing to keep her while abandoning her biological child—it fails to be appropriate or believable within a realistic context. There are numerous logical inconsistencies that break the plausibility of the narrative: a 4-pound-14-ounce premature infant would not be kept in a standard bassinet or immediately discharged without special care; a husband (Paul) would not sleep in a waiting room through an emergency C-section and an entire day without ever seeing his baby or learning its gender until driving home; a baby would not be taken out of a car seat to nurse in a mother's lap during a drive home from the hospital; and a mother's abrupt, unbothered decision to abandon her fragile biological newborn simply because the switched baby is heavier and "certain" lacks sufficient psychological grounding to feel earned rather than merely shocking.
